whatItDoes: Builds standard vCard (.vcf) contact cards in your browser. Fill in name, organization, phone, email, website, address, and a photo, and the tool generates a standards-compliant VCard 3.0 file ready to download or copy.
whyItExists: Sharing contact information as a structured VCard lets people save your details to their address book in one tap. Manually writing .vcf files is error-prone, so a generator guarantees valid formatting for every field.
whoShouldUse: Professionals sharing digital business cards, event organizers distributing attendee contacts, website owners adding contact-save links, and anyone who needs a shareable .vcf file.
useCases: Generate a personal business card to share on email signatures and social profiles
Create a QR-coded VCard so visitors can save your details by scanning
Build contact files for team directories and event badge systems
Export a clean vCard from scattered contact details
instructions: Enter the contact name and optional organization and title
Add phone, email, website, and address fields as needed
Optionally attach a photo for the vCard
Click Generate VCard to render the .vcf output
Copy the output or download it as a .vcf file
Import the file into Contacts, Outlook, or Gmail to verify it
examples:
BEGIN:VCARD
VERSION:3.0
N:Doe;John;;;
FN:John Doe
TEL;TYPE=WORK,VOICE:+1 555 0100
EMAIL:john.doe@example.com
ORG:DevStackIO
END:VCARD
A card with an address adds: ADR;TYPE=WORK:;;100 Main St;Springfield;IL;62701;US
A card with a website adds: URL;TYPE=WORK:https://example.com
A card with a photo adds: PHOTO;ENCODING=b;TYPE=JPEG:<base64 data>
bestPractices: Use the FN (formatted name) field so the card displays the exact name you want
Include a photo at a small size to keep the .vcf file lightweight
Test the generated file in your address book before publishing it
Combine with a QR code for quick mobile saving
commonMistakes: Forgetting the FN field, which many contact apps use as the primary display name
Using non-standard field names that importers ignore
Embedding a very large photo that makes the vCard slow to open
Adding line breaks inside field values, which break the VCard format
faq: Which VCard version does this generate? — VCard 3.0 (RFC 2426), which is compatible with Gmail, Outlook, Apple Contacts, and most address books.
Can I add custom fields? — The generator covers the most common fields; for niche properties you can edit the raw output before saving.
Is my data uploaded anywhere? — No. Everything is built locally in your browser.
Can I use this in a QR code? — Yes, paste the generated VCard into a QR generator or use our QR Code Generator with the contact payload.
features: Name, organization, phone, email, website, and address fields
